hero.subtitle: Marysville's warehouses, ag operations, and roadside job sites along 10th Street and B Street see their share of on-the-job injuries. We can review your workers' comp and third-party options at no cost, so you understand what claims may be available to you.

about.title: Marysville Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Yuba County's economy runs on distribution centers, farming operations, and small manufacturing shops scattered around Marysville, and with that work comes real risk — forklift accidents, falls from loading docks, repetitive strain, and equipment injuries are common claims we handle. If you were hurt while working, California law usually routes your claim through workers' compensation regardless of fault, but that's not always the end of the story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury — say, a delivery mishap near 5th Street or E Street — you may have a separate claim against that third party on top of any comp benefits. Our team can review both angles of your case at no cost, so you understand what options are actually available to you before deadlines pass.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, docks, or scaffolding
about.ctaText: Get your free case review — no obligation.

items.title: We Untangle Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — a contractor, equipment maker, or another driver — can open a separate claim. We can help sort out which path, or both, apply to your situation.

items.title: We Understand the 30-Day Reporting Clock
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your benefits. We review your case quickly so you can act before that deadline slips by.

items.title: We Know Retaliation Is Illegal — and We Take It Seriously
items.desc: If you're worried about reporting an injury because of how your employer might react, know that retaliation for filing a claim is against California law. We can advise you on protecting your job while pursuing what you're owed.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near 10th Street — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' comp is your primary remedy against your employer regardless of fault. But if a third party — like a subcontractor, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer — contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate injury claim. We can review the specifics and explain which options apply to you.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury and to file a claim?
items.answer: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. If a third-party claim is involved, that claim typically carries a two-year deadline from the date of injury. Missing either window can limit your options, so it helps to move quickly.

items.question: Will you charge me anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free. Attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for you.
